chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isa al-Nahrawari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who recognizes Allah and magnifies Him, prevents his mouth from speech, his belly from food, and excuses his self with fasting and standing (for prayer).'

They said, 'By our fathers and our mothers, O Rasool-Allah! Are these the friends of Allah?' He said: 'Indeed, the friends of Allah were silent, so their silence was remembrance; they looked, so their looking was a lesson; they spoke, so their speaking was wisdom; they walked, so their walking among the people was a blessing. Had it not been for the terms ordained upon them, their spirits would not have remained in their bodies out of fear of punishment and longing for reward.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs and characteristics of the friends of Allah (awliya) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the spiritual state of the *Awliya* (Friends of God), linking their physical restraint in speech and consumption to a profound internal awareness of the Divine. The text highlights that their silence is active remembrance (*dhikr*) and their gaze is contemplative (*i'tibar*), reflecting a state of constant vigilance where their souls remain eager for reward yet fearful of punishment, preventing them from settling comfortably in their bodies until their appointed term expires.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Isa Al Hureyri, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who recognises Allahazwj and Hisazwj Magnificence would prevent his mouth from the speech, and his belly from the food, and excuses himself with the Fasting and the standing (for Salāt)’.

They said, ‘By our fathers and our mothers, O Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>! Are they the friends of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘The friends of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> observed silence, so their silence was a Remembrance (of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>); and they looked around, so their looking around was a lesson; and they spoke, so their speaking was wisdom; and they walked, so their walking between the people was a Blessing. Had it not been for the term which had been Ordained upon them, their spirits would not have stayed in their bodies out of fear from the Punishment and desire to the Rewards’.
en.sarwar: 25. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Isa al-Nahriri from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever comes to know Allah and realizes His greatness does not allow his mouth to speak or his stomach to eat. He engages his soul in fasting and standing for prayer until it is clean and exhausted.’

They then said, ‘May Allah keep the souls of our parents in service for your cause, O Messenger of Allah, is it not that such people are close friends of Allah?’ The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘The close friends of Allah kept silent and it was considered speaking of Allah, they looked and it served as a good lesson, they spoke and it was wisdom, they walked and that was blessings among the people. Had it not been for the appointed time of their life span that was written down for them, their spirit would not have remained in their bodies for fear of torment and the desire for rewards.’”
